items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: So there was one time, the drummer, Tommy, Tommy Johnson I believe his name was, he had trouble with his alimony payments. And they got a call the police were going to come and get him. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4- Anyhow he split and left the drums there.

ctx.x: Okay. But did you ever play with your father?

Oh yeah. Oh boy. I mean that’s how I started playing music. I started playing, I always took piano lessons. Like if you have a dad and mom and aunts, it’s either guitar or piano, and back in those days you were like really country if you played the guitar. If you were a black kid playing guitar, forget it. I didn’t want that image, I was too cool for that. I didn’t want to play the piano either but there was nothing I could do. So like from 10 to 14, that’s what I did, I took piano lessons. And I really enjoyed…

Anyhow he split and left the drums there. And then my dad was stuck. So I said, “Hey dad, you know, I know all these songs.” I was 14 and I was still in junior high school. And I was at an Air Force base with my dad and so I started doing these gigs at the Air Force base with my music teacher, because there was a young music teacher in the schools in Massachusetts during those days, the forties and fifties, you had a music teacher. And this guy played the trumpet in my dad’s band. So it was like a real secret…
